why: The broker-backed conformance cases all drive the same extension: echo, add, boom, big, session, slow, hang, plus a few config knobs and a variable. Declaring it here means every SDK builds the SAME extension instead of four hand-written ones that can drift — which is exactly what happened with the config decoder, where all four had the same defect and every suite passed.

tools.name: echo
tools.why: the workhorse: returns `echo:<msg>` so a caller can prove its arguments arrived

tools.name: add
tools.why: returns a structured `data` result rather than text

tools.name: boom
tools.why: returns a business error, so error mapping is exercised

tools.name: big
tools.description: returns more text than the content cap allows
tools.why: exceeds the tool-content cap, which must be refused rather than truncated

tools.name: session
tools.description: echoes the session name it was called with
tools.why: proves the agent threads the session name into the call

tools.name: slow
tools.why: answers after a delay, so a caller can prove request timeouts are bounded

tools.name: hang
tools.why: waits until cancelled, which is how interrupt is tested

config.name: token
config.description: a credential; never returned to a client
